answer: The store converts 2.02% of sessions, below the 2.77% fashion average (DY-FASHION: Dynamic Yield, June 2026, as quoted by Shopify). Estimated at this store's device mix (81.0% of desktop and mobile sessions are mobile, against the 69.9% Contentsquare reports across all sites, assumed for the fashion row), the fair comparison is about 2.56%, so the store is 0.54 points behind, worth about $27,473 in the period; the gap sits on mobile, while desktop is within range.

site_total.estimate_note: The adjusted figure is an estimate: it assumes the fashion row has the device blend Contentsquare reports across all websites (69.9% mobile) and Contentsquare's retail desktop to mobile ratio.

device_mix_adjustment.formula: DY-FASHION x (site mobile share x CS-MOB + site desktop share x CS-DESK) / (0.699 x CS-MOB + 0.301 x CS-DESK)
assumptions: The fashion row (DY-FASHION) has the device blend Contentsquare reports across all websites in 2026: 69.9% mobile, 30.1% desktop (CS-MIX). Neither Dynamic Yield nor Shopify publishes a device mix for the fashion figure.
Fashion's desktop to mobile ratio matches Contentsquare's retail rows (CS-DESK 3.7%, CS-MOB 2.0%).
device_mix_adjustment.benchmark_mobile_share_source: CS-MIX, assumed for the fashion row
device_mix_adjustment.reading: If the fashion row has Contentsquare's all-site device blend, the heavier mobile mix explains about 0.21 of the 0.75 point gap to the published average, and the remaining 0.54 points are the store's own. If fashion shoppers are more mobile than the all-site blend, more of the gap is mix; if less, more of it is the store's.

mix_vs_rate_since_prior.reading: The store rate fell 0.29 points against the prior 30 days. 81% of that is mix: Paid Social grew from 11.9% to 23.0% of sessions at a 0.48% rate, so every higher-converting channel lost share. The drop is a targeting question for the paid social team, not a site problem; the gap to the benchmark is the site's.

what_the_mix_hides: Email converts 6.48% of sessions and returning visitors 3.91%, against 0.48% for Paid Social and 1.32% for new visitors. A single industry average blends all of these, which is why the store is judged on its own device mix and channels are judged against their own history.

cro_projects.where_to_start: The overall case. Desktop is within range, so the store-wide gap sits on mobile: start with the mobile project.
